auth.forbidden: You have no role for this section
auth.notConfiguredHint: No OIDC issuer: oidc.authority in public/config.json is empty. The panel is behind SSO on every contour — ask whoever deployed it.

errors.conflict: Conflict: the configuration changed or is contradictory

common.reasonPlaceholder: The justification goes to the audit journal

dashboard.killSwitchActive: Kill switch is on — sending is stopped
dashboard.killSwitchWithOtp: All traffic is stopped, including CRITICAL_OTP

batches.streamIdHint: The stream the send is made on behalf of: its quotas, limits and quiet hours apply to the message. The identifier from «Входящие потоки», e.g. payroll

send.singleHint: The text comes from a published template — one a second person has already reviewed (FR-4.2)
send.bulkHint: Columns by header name: the address column of the channel (msisdn / email / pushToken), clientId and externalId are reserved, every other column becomes a merge variable. Re-uploading the same file is safe
send.estimateWarning: This is a real send to customers. An estimate is an estimate: tariffs and provider health may change between confirming and sending
send.fileFailures: Rows of the file that could not be read
send.channelHint: Which channel the message goes out on. The recipient needs an address for it and the template needs text for it
send.trafficClassHint: Empty leaves it to the stream. CRITICAL_OTP is not held by the kill switch and does not wait for quiet hours
send.msisdnHint: The number as 998XXXXXXXXX — no plus sign, spaces or dashes
send.emailHint: The recipient's address. If it is on the suppression list the message is rejected at acceptance
send.pushTokenHint: The device token. A dead one is refused by the platform and lands on the suppression list by itself
send.clientIdHint: Optional. It is what lets a ban placed on the whole customer, rather than on one address, stop the send
send.variablesHint: Values of the template's merge fields: a NAME column fills {NAME} in the text. Unfilled ones are listed in the estimate
send.fileHint: A CSV with columns by header name: the channel's address column (msisdn / email / pushToken) plus any variable columns. Case matters: a NAME column fills {NAME}, a name column does not
send.templatesTruncated: There are more templates than the list holds — narrow the channel

streams.name: Name
streams.streamIdHint: The identifier every submission of this source system will carry. Permanent: it cannot be changed after registration. Lowercase Latin only: PlayMobile is refused, playmobile is not.
streams.integrationTypeHint: Which transport this stream submits over: REST, Kafka or both
streams.credentialsRefHint: A reference to the secret, never the secret: env:NAME or prop:key. The Hub resolves it on use and stores no value (SEC-04)
streams.defaultChannelHint: Default channel for this stream's messages when the source system names none
streams.defaultProviderHint: The stream's preferred provider. Routing still fails over to the reserve when it is unavailable (FR-6.3)
streams.trafficClassHint: The default class. Queue isolation follows from it: a bulk campaign may not take turns away from OTP (TC-01)
streams.priorityHint: Default priority within the traffic class
streams.dailyCountHint: Ceiling of messages per day. Over it, the rule below decides: refuse, or only raise an alert
streams.monthlyCountHint: Ceiling of messages per month, counted independently of the daily one
streams.dailyCostHint: Ceiling of spend per day by provider tariffs rather than by message count
streams.monthlyCostHint: Ceiling of spend per month by provider tariffs
streams.quotaBehaviorHint: BLOCK refuses messages over the quota; ALERT_ONLY lets them through and raises an alert
streams.tpsHint: How many messages a second the stream may submit. A limit on ingest, not on sending (IR-02)
streams.perMinuteHint: The per-minute ceiling; it smooths bursts that slip through the per-second one
streams.perRecipientPerHourHint: How many messages one address gets per hour. It protects the customer from a flood, not the Hub from load (FR-5.4)
streams.quietStartHint: Start of the quiet-hours window, HH:MM. Messages inside it are held or refused by the rule below (FR-5.3)
streams.quietEndHint: End of the quiet-hours window, HH:MM. The window may cross midnight
streams.quietZoneHint: Timezone of the window. Usually Asia/Tashkent — the window is the customer's local time, not the server's
streams.quietBehaviorHint: DEFER holds the message until the window closes, REJECT refuses it at once. OTP does not observe quiet hours
streams.clearQuietHoursHint: Removes the quiet-hours window altogether. Clearing the fields above does not — that means 'leave unchanged'
streams.nameHint: The human-readable name shown in lists and reports. The identifier is the field above and, unlike the name, never changes
streams.streamIdFormat: Lowercase Latin letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore only, 2-64 characters. For example: mobile-app

providers.fallbackOrderHint: Provider codes in failover order; Enter adds one
providers.adapterTypeHint: Which adapter serves the profile. The list is what this contour deployed for the selected channel; adding a type is a release (AR-04)
providers.adapterTypeEmpty: No adapter for the selected channel is deployed on this contour
providers.deleteConfirm: Delete the profile? Rejected while anything still routes through the provider
providers.testSendHint: The send goes through the normal pipeline with the TEST flag: stream quotas, channel filters, provider credentials (FR-7.4)
providers.pinProviderHint: Pins the send to one provider, excluding the others
providers.subject: Subject
providers.codeHint: The profile's permanent code: routing, statistics and the provider's own reports all use it. It cannot be changed. UPPERCASE Latin only — unlike a stream identifier.
providers.channelHint: The channel this profile serves. An SMS provider cannot become an email one
providers.weightHint: Share of traffic under weighted balancing. Unused by the other strategies
providers.perMessageHint: Price of a whole message. For SMS the per-segment price is the accurate one
providers.perSegmentHint: Price of one SMS segment. A long message is several segments, and the estimate counts them (§18.3)
providers.balancingStrategyHint: How a provider is picked from the list: by priority, round robin, by weight or by lowest cost
providers.quietHoursChannelHint: The channel's quiet-hours window. A stream may have its own, and that one wins because it knows the customer's timezone
providers.pushPlatformHint: The device platform, not the adapter. A token belongs to one platform, and the adapter is chosen by it
providers.subjectHint: The subject line; SMS and push have none
providers.testTextHint: The text of the test message. Free-form on purpose: what is being checked is the transport, not the wording
providers.testStreamIdHint: The stream the check is made on behalf of: its quotas and filters apply (FR-7.4)
providers.testChannelHint: Which channel the check goes out on. The message really does reach the address given
providers.codeFormat: UPPERCASE Latin letters, digits and underscore only, 2-32 characters. For example: PLAYMOBILE

routing.dryRunHint: Nothing is sent: the message is built in memory and run through the real Router against the real configuration
routing.matchStreamIdHint: The rule matches this stream only. Empty means any stream
routing.matchTrafficClassHint: The rule matches this traffic class only. Empty means any class
routing.minPriorityHint: The rule matches messages of at least this priority
routing.matchChannelHint: The rule matches messages of this channel only. Empty means any channel
routing.actionChannelHint: Which channel the matched messages go out on
routing.dryRunStreamIdHint: The stream the route is computed for: different streams have different policies and limits
routing.dryRunRecipientHint: The address is needed to compute the route; nothing is sent anywhere
routing.dryRunChannelHint: Channel of the hypothetical message. Empty lets the Hub choose
routing.dryRunTrafficClassHint: Traffic class of the hypothetical message: which rule matches depends on it
routing.textForSegmentsHint: The text is only used to count segments and cost — it is not sent anywhere

templates.importHint: Columns by header name: code, channel, locale, text are required. Publishing needs an approver different from the author (FR-4.2)
templates.dropCsv: Drop a CSV file or click to choose
templates.ownVersionHint: Publication is done by a second person: you authored this version (FR-4.2)
templates.draftHint: Only a DRAFT may be rewritten; publication is done by a second person (FR-4.2)
templates.codeHint: The template code from «Шаблоны», e.g. OTP_LOGIN. The text comes only from it — free text cannot be sent from here (FR-4.2)
templates.newCodeHint: The template's permanent name: source systems refer to it by this, and it stays in the history of every message sent from it. It cannot be changed later. UPPERCASE Latin only.
templates.localeFieldHint: The language variant of the template. A version published in that very language is required, or the estimate refuses
templates.channelHint: The template's channel: an SMS template cannot go out as an email. It cannot be changed later
templates.directionHint: A free-form note on what the template is for — service notices, marketing. It only affects the catalogue filter
templates.ownerHint: Who owns the wording: whom to go to when it needs changing
templates.textHint: The text of the version. Variables are written as {NAME}; an unfilled one stops the message on a real send and simply stays visible in the preview
templates.subjectHint: The subject line. Email only — SMS and push have none
templates.htmlHint: The HTML alternative of the email. It travels alongside the text: text is always required, HTML only next to it (EM-01)
templates.mappingProviderHint: Code of the provider the template is registered with
templates.providerTemplateIdHint: The template's identifier on the provider's side. Needed where the provider requires the wording to be registered first (FR-4.5)
templates.approvedHint: The provider has confirmed the registration. Until it has, a send on this template may be refused
templates.previewVariablesHint: Values for the preview. Unfilled ones stay visible as {NAME} and are listed — the preview is deliberately not strict
templates.codeFormat: UPPERCASE Latin letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore only, 2-64 characters. For example: OTP_LOGIN

suppressions.addHint: Exactly one of address and client ID; the address is validated and hashed on the server
suppressions.importHint: Columns by header name: channel and reason are required, plus one of address / clientId. Re-uploading a file is safe
suppressions.removeConfirm: Remove the entry — opt-in after opt-out?
suppressions.channelHint: Channel of the ban. Empty bans the address on every channel at once
suppressions.addressHint: The address is validated and hashed on the server: the list keeps the hash, never the address
suppressions.clientIdHint: Bans the whole customer rather than one address. Given instead of an address, not alongside it
suppressions.reasonHint: Why the address is banned. It shows in the list and explains how it got there
suppressions.validUntilHint: When the ban expires. Empty means never
suppressions.checkChannelHint: The channel the address is checked for
suppressions.checkAddressHint: The address to check. It is not stored — only hashed to look the ban up
suppressions.checkClientIdHint: Check for bans placed on the whole customer

audit.truncated: The export stopped at the 50 000-row ceiling — narrow the period

administration.releaseConfirm: Release the kill switch? The flow resumes where it stopped
administration.activateHint: The saga holds back everything it is allowed to hold; CRITICAL_OTP keeps flowing until stopped explicitly
administration.deleteParameterConfirm: Delete the parameter — return to the deployment default?
administration.ssoMappingHint: The Hub stores no users and no passwords: identity comes from the corporate SSO, the group → role mapping is deployment configuration (config.json) and is read-only here
administration.ssoMappingEmpty: No mapping set — a group named like a role passes as is
administration.killSwitchReasonHint: Required. The entry 'everything stopped at 03:14' is worth reading only if it says why (FR-7.3)
administration.includeOtpHint: By default one-time codes keep going. The checkbox stops them too — which cuts customers out of the app
administration.keyHint: The parameter's name. It overrides the deployment default of the same name; the name cannot be changed later
administration.valueHint: The value that beats the deployment default. Deleting the parameter restores that default
administration.descriptionHint: Why the parameter exists: whoever finds it in six months has nothing but this line to go on
